port_unverifiable.description: A provider native failure: the declared port cannot be cross-checked on a stopped instance. alias names the configured instance, adb_port the declared port, and instances the discovered instance, which reported no port.

adb_path_encoding_invalid.description: A provider native failure: the discovered adb path is not UTF-8. alias names the configured instance, other_path the discovered adb (lossy), adb_path the declared adb when one is declared, and instances the discovered instance.

path_encoding_invalid.description: A provider native failure: a vision path is not UTF-8.

policy_driver_reference_leaked.description: A reference to the Runtime host outlived the policy driver at close.

policy_driver_signal_poisoned.description: The policy driver's signal lock is poisoned.

policy_driver_wake_missing.description: The policy driver woke without work.

policy_recompute_trigger_missing.description: The policy driver took recompute work without its trigger.

policy_monitor_request_retried.description: A request of actingd's policy monitor to its own Runtime got no receipt header within policy.monitor.io_timeout_ms (io_kind timed_out, or would_block); the monitor sends it again on a fresh connection after retry_after_ms. attempts counts the failures in a row, limit_count is policy.monitor.retry_limit.
policy_monitor_request_retried.common_causes: The host is overloaded (CPU near 100 %) or the Runtime's ledger writer stalls longer than the monitor's I/O timeout.
policy_monitor_request_retried.handling: None while the failures stay under the limit. If it recurs, lower the host load or raise policy.monitor.io_timeout_ms.

policy_monitor_retries_exhausted.description: actingd's policy monitor gave up: after limit_count retries in a row (policy.monitor.retry_limit), one more request to its own Runtime got no receipt header in time. actingd then stops with that request's failure.
policy_monitor_retries_exhausted.common_causes: The Runtime did not answer its local IPC for longer than the retries cover: a sustained host overload, or a Runtime that hangs.
policy_monitor_retries_exhausted.handling: Check the host load and the Runtime's ledger writer, then start the Runtime again. If the host is expected to stall this long, raise policy.monitor.retry_limit, retry_backoff_max_ms or io_timeout_ms.

policy_monitor_runtime_identity_changed.description: The policy monitor's connection reached a Runtime other than the one actingd hosts: the Runtime info file names another owner epoch or process id. actingd stops.

policy_monitor_config_invalid.description: actingd refused its configuration file: a policy.monitor value is outside its range.
policy_monitor_config_invalid.handling: Correct policy.monitor as contracts/actingd-check-config.md describes it.

provider_native_failed.description: Provider startup failed in the device layer and the device error names no registered code; device_category names the device failure's category when the device error has one, and a foreign_other_error link carries the device's text. mumu_root names the configured MuMu folder of a failed discovery when one is configured.

config_subsystem_configured.description: The configuration manifest reports a subsystem the configuration file configures: its flag is on or its section is present.

config_subsystem_configured_off.description: The configuration manifest reports a subsystem the configuration file turns off with its flag; an env_overrides subsystem carries each ignored ACTINGCOMMAND_* variable as a note link of env_override_ignored.

config_subsystem_flag_absent.description: The configuration manifest reports a subsystem whose flag the configuration file does not name, so its default applies; an env_overrides subsystem carries each ignored ACTINGCOMMAND_* variable as a note link of env_override_ignored.

config_subsystem_section_absent.description: The configuration manifest reports a subsystem off because the configuration file has no section for it.

config_subsystem_always_on.description: The configuration manifest reports a subsystem the Runtime always runs; count is the number of allowed client identities when the governance subsystem restricts them.

config_subsystem_discovery_bound.description: The configuration manifest reports a discovery subsystem on: count instances are bound by instance_index or instance_name.

config_subsystem_discovery_unbound.description: The configuration manifest reports a discovery subsystem off: no instance is bound by instance_index or instance_name.

device_config_invalid.description: actingd refused its configuration (#398 R1 RD-3i): an instance's device fields do not fit its device kind, for example capture_backend scrcpy on an emulator instance. Every configured instance is an emulator until RD-1b adds the key device.kind.

config_load.description: check-config and unlock-owner stage: loading the configuration file (v1 token load).

config_assemble.description: check-config stage: assembling the configuration (v1 token assemble).

config_vision.description: check-config stage: listing the vision root (v1 token vision).

config_validate.description: check-config stage: validating the assembled host configuration (v1 token validate).

resource_package.description: check-config stage: admitting the resource packages.

policy_state.description: check-config stage: previewing the catalog plan against the ledger.

policy_initialization.description: actingd stage: activating the configured catalog and running the first policy cycle.

policy_bootstrap.description: actingd stage: choosing between the policy driver and the plain monitor.

policy_monitor_setup.description: actingd stage: connecting the policy monitor and starting the policy driver.

policy_closeout_driver.description: actingd stage of the policy closeout: the policy driver's result (FATAL token driver).

policy_closeout_monitor.description: actingd stage of the policy closeout: the policy monitor's result (FATAL token monitor).

policy_closeout_shutdown.description: actingd stage of the policy closeout: the policy driver's shutdown (FATAL token shutdown).

policy_closeout_host_close.description: actingd stage of the policy closeout: closing the Runtime host (FATAL token close).
